[RTCT.7.6] **RT-safety is checked at LOAD, not at evaluation.** A `.dsc` whose
dialect resolves `realtime` **must** be refused at load if it contains a call
to an operation the runtime does not hold to be RT-safe — bounded time, bounded
space, no allocation. The refusal is a load error, alongside the other
capability refusals, and names the operation.

**Why load and not first fire.** A per-activation check discovers the breach
only when the offending rule happens to fire, which may be days in. Until then
the artefact has been accepted, `ds_engine_go_live` has succeeded, and the
deployment reads as conforming — so the failure arrives as a trap in the field
rather than as a refusal at deploy, on the one profile whose entire purpose is
that its costs are known **before** it runs.

It also cannot be reconciled with the contract itself. `[RTCT.7.2]` enforces
caps against declared bounds, and a WCET bound over a rule set containing an
unbounded operation is not a bound that was ever satisfiable. Admitting the
artefact and trapping later asserts a guarantee the artefact cannot keep.

**The set of RT-safe operations is the runtime's to declare and is not an
author surface.** An author writes the same language under `realtime`; what
changes is which of it the profile admits, which is `[LCAP]`'s model and not a
second dialect.
